equation.name: How far a hot star lights up the gas around it
equation.formula: R = if Q <= 0 or n <= 0 then 0 else cbrt(3 * Q / (4 * pi * n * n * alpha_B))

alpha_B.name: case B recombination coefficient at 10⁴ K

R.name: radius of the glowing ionised ball

source.text: Osterbrock, D. E. and Ferland, G. J. 2006, Astrophysics of Gaseous Nebulae and Active Galactic Nuclei, 2nd edn, University Science Books

explain.curious: A hot star lights a glowing bubble in the gas round it, out to where every ionising photon has been used up keeping the gas ionised. Thinner gas, bigger bubble.
explain.science: Ionisation balance in a uniform medium: photons emitted equal recombinations to excited levels (case B) inside the sphere.

equation.name: Red glow of hydrogen recombining
equation.formula:
E_Ha = h * c / lambda_Ha
P = share * E_Ha * N

share.name: red hydrogen photons per recombination (case B, 10⁴ K)

source.text: Osterbrock, D. E. and Ferland, G. J. 2006, Astrophysics of Gaseous Nebulae and Active Galactic Nuclei, 2nd edn, University Science Books

explain.curious: Each time an electron falls back onto a proton it cascades down the energy ladder, and nearly half the time one step gives out the red light of hydrogen alpha. That is why glowing nebulae are red.
explain.science: Case B at 10⁴ K: 0.45 Hα photons per recombination, so L(Hα) = 1.37×10⁻¹⁹ W per recombination per second. For an ionisation-bounded nebula the recombination rate equals the ionising photon rate.

equation.name: How far a cast-off shell has spread

source.text: Kwok, S., Purton, C. R. and Fitzgerald, P. M. 1978, On the origin of planetary nebulae, ApJ 219, L125

explain.curious: The gas a dying star throws off coasts outwards at a steady speed, so a ring nebula's size is a clock: measure it and its speed and you know its age.
explain.science: In the interacting-winds picture the swept-up shell of a planetary nebula expands at a nearly constant speed of tens of km/s over its visible life.

equation.name: How big a supernova's blast wave has grown
equation.formula:
rho = mu_H * m_H * n
v = sqrt(2 * E / M)
r_free = v * t
r_sweep = cbrt(3 * M / (4 * pi * rho))
e51 = E / E51
n_cc = n * cc
t_pds = c_pds * yr * e51 ^ (3/14) * n_cc ^ (-4/7)
r_sedov = max(xi * (E * t * t / rho) ^ (1/5), r_sweep)
r_pds = 14 * pc * e51 ^ (2/7) * n_cc ^ (-3/7)
R = if r_free < r_sweep then r_free else if t < t_pds then r_sedov else r_pds * (4 * t / (3 * t_pds) - 1/3) ^ (3/10)

n.name: hydrogen atoms per cubic metre around it

mu_H.name: mass per hydrogen atom, with helium

source.text: Cioffi, D. F., McKee, C. F. and Bertschinger, E. 1988, Dynamics of radiative supernova remnants, ApJ 334, 252

explain.curious: A supernova's blast coasts at first, then slows as it sweeps up gas, then cools and ploughs on as a thin shell until it is no faster than the gas around it.
explain.science: Free expansion at √(2E/M) until the swept mass equals the ejecta; the Sedov-Taylor blast wave R = 1.15 (E t²/ρ)^⅕; after shell formation Cioffi, McKee and Bertschinger's pressure-driven snowplough. Solar metallicity; uniform surroundings.
